amenitiesDescription:
Spa and wellness: A ground-floor spa with steam room, sauna, hot tub, salon, and massage treatment room, opening onto a terrace and a pool set into the planting. One level up, a fitness studio with a private training room, lounge, and locker rooms sits next to a vitality pool on the landscaped deck.

Rooftop: A pool deck open on every side, with a sundeck and lounge area. An event space with a cocktail room and outdoor lounge is reservable for private gatherings.

Ground floor and beach: Twin reflecting ponds with private floating cabanas sit between the building and the dune, with a recreational lawn, outdoor kitchen, and lawn lounge alongside. The Club Room holds lounge seating, a library, and a communal dining table.

Services: Front-desk reception and concierge around the clock, 24-hour valet, an on-site property manager, beach and pool chair service, package receiving, covered bicycle storage, and electric vehicle charging in the garage.
description: Twenty-five oceanfront residences at 9317 Collins Avenue in Surfside. Twelve stories by Arquitectonica for Multiplan, with Carla Guilhem interiors, a full spa level, and a rooftop pool. From $5M, delivery 2027.

investmentThesis:
Surfside holds new construction to low-rise, low-density zoning, the same constraint that makes the Four Seasons Surf Club campus and Arte Surfside effectively unrepeatable. Ocean House is one of very few ground-up condominiums entitled inside that envelope. Scarcity here is a function of the code, not of marketing.

This is Multiplan's third boutique condominium in the Miami Beach corridor, following 57 Ocean and Ocean Park South Beach. Chief executive Marcelo Kingston runs the Miami arm. Arquitectonica has been building in the city since 1977, and Fort-Brescia took this commission directly.

The buyer this building is aimed at wants oceanfront square footage and a short owner roster without a hotel operator on the deed. There is no flag and no resort levy. What is here is scaled to twenty-five owners, not to a sales brochure.

name: Ocean House Surfside
parking: Garage with 24-hour valet; EV charging stations
residenceContent:
Twelve stories of transparent glass on a beachfront parcel where Collins Avenue meets 93rd Street. Bernardo Fort-Brescia drew the building as a set of curves rather than a stack of floor plates. Wraparound balconies do the structural talking: clear glass railings, up to twelve feet deep, with wood-like ceiling accents that carry the eye out over the sand. Arrival is under a covered porte-cochere and through a double-height lobby of wood and stone. A walkway runs from the dune line through a landscaped garden into an outdoor lounge finished in natural stone, and every home is reached by a private keyed elevator opening into its own vestibule.

Homes run from two bedrooms to five, plus a two-level penthouse on the top floor with its own oceanfront rooftop. Ceilings hold at roughly ten feet through the building and reach twelve in the penthouse. Floor-to-ceiling impact glass slides open onto the terraces, so the living space reads continuously from the interior stone flooring out to the balcony. Views run east to the Atlantic, south down the beach toward Miami Beach, and west across Biscayne Bay to the Downtown skyline.

Interiors are by Carla Guilhem, whose practice splits between yachts and private homes. The material palette is deliberately short: wood, natural stone, and little else. Kitchens pair custom European cabinetry with Gaggenau appliances and a Silestone island with a waterfall edge. Bathrooms carry double vanities, glass-enclosed rainfall showers, freestanding tubs, and stone floors. The penthouse steps up the specification with Poliform cabinetry and Fantini fixtures, and adds a cinema, a game room, staff quarters with a service kitchen, an ensuite spa with private steam and sauna, and a six-car garage.
